note: SEPARATE evidence cell from webkit-engine (Playwright). Per I-20, no webkit verdict is copied here; every row below was measured in REAL Safari via safaridriver.
env: dev server UP, API-LESS (no mongo) — data-backed surfaces render empty by environment, not defect

viewports.name: widest
viewports.displayNote: the OS did NOT clamp the window; Safari accepted 3440x1440 and innerWidth measured 3440. But the logical screen is only 2048x1152, so ~1392 CSS px of the window is OFF-SCREEN. The WebDriver WINDOW-snapshot path fails at this size (see snapshotFailure).

snapshotFailure.symptom: GET /session/<id>/screenshot at 3440x1440 returns a pixel-identical all-black 6880x2776 PNG (343548 bytes, sha256 914cfe439270b33121b2f3373bab10b9b9f25c3edfc52d0c547cf45d9863f6b4)
snapshotFailure.reproduction: 4 valid 6880px frames captured first (root/gradient/browse/blob), then every subsequent widest window-snapshot returned the black frame; 9 further attempts across 3 fresh sessions (incl. as the FIRST capture, and for the previously-good #/ control) all returned the same black frame
snapshotFailure.notAnAppBlank: the black frame is pure black while the page's own body background computes to rgb(38,0,27); an ELEMENT snapshot of <main> at the same instant returns 11.3-11.6 MB of real painted content. The page IS painted; the window-snapshot surface is not.
snapshotFailure.notACrash: no Safari/WebContent .ips written during any run; sessions closed cleanly
snapshotFailure.mitigation: generate/mix/extract widest PNGs are ELEMENT snapshots of <main> (3408x1288 CSS px, i.e. the viewport minus the 16px gutters). The failing window frames are preserved as <slug>-3440-windowsnap-black.png

consoleErrorLimitation: WebDriver classic cannot inject before load; window.onerror/unhandledrejection hooks were installed AFTER load, so early-boot errors are a DECLARED blind spot. Post-install error arrays were empty on all 21 cells — that is NOT a claim of zero boot errors.
